part.text:
Fixed. The fix mirrors the upstream resolution of fmt issue #2305/PR #2310, with two parts:

1. **`include/fmt/core.h`** (`specs_setter::on_zero`): the `0` flag now only forces `align::numeric` when no explicit alignment was given, so `{: <+06}` keeps left alignment instead of being silently overridden.

2. **`include/fmt/format.h`** (`float_writer::write_nonfinite`): since `'0'` fill still gets applied as padding, non-finite values now replace the `'0'` fill with `' '` so zero-padding "has no effect" on infinity/NaN, while width/alignment still apply.

Verified: `'{:+06}'` on NaN/inf now yields `'  +nan'` / `'  +inf'`, explicit alignments work (`{:<+06}` → `'+nan  '`, `{:^+06}` → `' +nan '`, `{:>+06}` → `'  +nan'`), and numeric zero-padding is unchanged (`{:+06}` on `120` → `'+00120'`). Full test suite passes: 18/18 ctest targets, including the previously failing `format_nan` and `format_infinity` tests.
